input.topic: DNA Replication: 3' End Of Growing Chain

expected.question_text: In an experiment investigating the mechanisms of DNA replication and repair in eukaryotes, a group of researchers aims to study the various enzymes involved in the process. The experiment is planned to provide a novel paradigm for the mechanisms by which the DNA replication machinery is coordinated with DNA repair proteins in response. The researchers design an in vitro assay mimicking DNA replication. They use purified proteins involved in replication and observe their actions on a synthetic DNA template. One of the target enzymes in the experiment is DNA polymerase. Which of the following is a fundamental function of this enzyme?
expected.explanation_header: The correct answer is Addition of deoxyribonucleotides to the 3′ hydroxyl group of a growing chain.
expected.explanation_footer:
https://d2vrujxrqm3l5p.cloudfront.net/90b7a7bc-530e-446e-94ec-1271e56de7e1.png DNA replication is a semiconservative process, meaning that for every new pair, there is one original strand and one new strand. This process begins with the initiation phase, where origin-binding proteins bind to the origin of replication, leading to the unwinding of the double helix by helicase , forming a replication fork. Single-stranded binding proteins stabilize the unwound DNA while topoisomerases alleviate tension and allow elongation to proceed. Primase generates RNA primers for DNA polymerases to initiate replication. During elongation, DNA polymerases (eg, DNA polymerase III in prokaryotes and DNA polymerase alpha, epsilon, and delta in eukaryotes) add deoxyribonucleotides to the 3′ hydroxyl group (3'-OH) of a growing chain , synthesizing DNA in the 5′ to 3′ direction. DNA polymerase III has 5’ to 3’ synthesis and 3’ to 5’ proofreading exonuclease. DNA polymerase alpha is a complex that has the DNA primase that creates the RNA primer, and then the polymerase alpha itself elongates approximately 20 nucleotides and passes off to DNA polymerase epsilon or delta. DNA polymerase epsilon elongates and proofreads on the leading strand. DNA polymerase delta elongates and proofreads on the lagging strand. The leading strand is synthesized continuously, whereas the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously in short segments, called Okazaki fragments. These fragments are later joined by DNA ligase after RNA primers are replaced by DNA. Termination occurs differently in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. In prokaryotes, replication ends when replication forks meet, whereas in eukaryotes, termination happens at telomere regions, which are repetitive sequences at chromosome ends.

DNA polymerase catalyzes the addition of deoxyribonucleotides to the 3′ hydroxyl group of a growing DNA chain during replication. This process occurs in the 5′ to 3′ direction and is essential for elongating the DNA strand.
